definitions.gloss: rescuer; person who rescues or saves others
definitions.explanation: A person who rescues others from danger, disaster, or emergency situations. Used in news reports, disaster coverage, and general descriptions of rescue activities.

examples.japanese: {救助者|きゅうじょしゃ}が{現場|げんば}に{駆|か}けつけた。
{救助者|きゅうじょしゃ}の{迅速|じんそく}な{対応|たいおう}のおかげで、{全員|ぜんいん}{無事|ぶじ}だった。
examples.english: Thanks to the rescuers' swift response, everyone was safe.

examples.japanese: {地震|じしん}の{後|あと}、{多|おお}くの{救助者|きゅうじょしゃ}が{被災地|ひさいち}に{入|はい}り、{瓦礫|がれき}の{下|した}から{生存者|せいぞんしゃ}を{探|さが}した。
examples.english: After the earthquake, many rescuers entered the disaster area and searched for survivors under the rubble.

notes:
Composed of {救助|きゅうじょ} (rescue) and {者|しゃ} (person). The {者|しゃ} suffix is productive in Japanese for forming agent nouns from action nouns.

While {救助者|きゅうじょしゃ} can refer to anyone who performs a rescue, in news and official contexts it often refers to trained professionals such as firefighters, coast guard members, or disaster relief workers. For civilians who happen to rescue someone, the phrase {救助|きゅうじょ}した{人|ひと} is also common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {救助者|きゅうじょしゃ}が{到着|とうちゃく}する: rescuers arrive
- {救助者|きゅうじょしゃ}を{派遣|はけん}する: to dispatch rescuers
- {救助者|きゅうじょしゃ}の{活動|かつどう}: rescue activities
- {救助者|きゅうじょしゃ}と{被救助者|ひきゅうじょしゃ}: rescuer and person being rescued

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {救助隊|きゅうじょたい}: rescue team — an organized group rather than an individual
- {救急隊員|きゅうきゅうたいいん}: paramedic, EMT — specifically emergency medical responders
- {救助|きゅうじょ}: rescue — the act itself
- {救援者|きゅうえんしゃ}: relief worker — focuses more on aid and support than immediate rescue from danger
